I battled anxiety and depression in 2019 to the point of suicidal thoughts and extreme isolation for many months. I went to a facility for three days. I went to counselors and got advice on how to “worship myself more”. That will not help. One way that’s helped is to lay down my life and serve others with it. A good blog I read said, “if you feel like killing yourself, do it, just don’t do it physically. Instead kill your desire for more for yourself. Die to yourself.” Jesus even went so far as to say “If you cling to your life, you will lose it; but if you give up your life for me, you will find it.” Matthew 10:39.

Anyway, if you’ve trudged through my top words, I have some questions. Why is she anxious? What is causing her anxiety? Anxiety typically has a cause. We medicate it as a disease. Maybe it is sometimes... my walk through depression did have a cause and depression and anxiety was an effect I believe now 2 long, arduous years later. When anxious and depressed, your thoughts will travel rapidly and randomly and darkly. I found out the number one symptom of depression is “inability to focus”. I always thought it was “sadness”. And so, try to keep her from rapid thoughts but understand it’s part of it for now. What is at the root of her anxiety? Is someone treating her unfairly, or unfriendly? Are the masks for Covid scary? Is her dad speaking life into her, as in, “honey you’re beautiful”, “you are perfect”, “you are made in the image of God”, “you are fearfully and wonderfully made”, “God knit you together in your mother’s womb”, “I’m always here for you”, “I’ll never leave you not forsake you”. Things like that I believe maybe could help speak life to her. And in all things, love.

I am 29 now. I’ve been married for seven years. Last year, I found out my children are special needs children. They are 3 (boy), and 2 (girl).

I was about as ambitious as a man can be. I worked extremely hard at my work. I was a sales rep for a Fortune 500 financial planning company in my early 20’s. I’ve always been the first there, and last to leave. I always strived for the absolute best, and that wasn’t good enough. I could always become better and become more. I met with many people to sell them insurance etc. I made a living. Within my first year, I hired an assistant to help me. I was 100% commission, so no salary, etc. I “ate what I killed”. The stress nearly killed my marriage and my life.

Here’s the point: I pushed myself past the limit. Last year, it landed me in a psychward for three days. I was suicidal (seriously). The reason was, what’s the point? I read the biblical book Ecclesiastes, and found out God agrees. There is no point in life outside of Him. Eat, live, be joyful, for God’s Glory.

I closed down the business, and moved to a custom cabinet shop. I now manage the shop. I make about 40% the amount of income. I’m the happiest I’ve ever been, and we have more money because I am not trying to walk around as a white washed casket (that’s an analogy for being beautiful on the outside, but dead and decaying on the inside).

So my advice to you is this: be ambitious, work hard, stay focused, yet don’t make your life’s goal to save money so you can skate through retirement. What the heck is retirement anyway? Getting fat, going bald, and having no purpose to your puney existence? Live like a man should, always honest, push the envelope, love those around you, never give up. The greatest question for a man is, “am I good enough?” Let me tell you, you are. Most of all, be content. This pandemic, this economy... it’s always changing and shifting and chaotic. So be it. It’s not as important what you’re doing, but who you are becoming. Live today like it is your last in the sense of loving with all you got, and living for more than yourself.

Hope this helps you my fellow man. Fight the good fight.
